content.title: Duke basketball vs St. John's final: Blue Devils hang on, advance to Elite 8
content.text: Updated March 27, 2026, 9:29 p.m. ETWASHINGTON, D.C. — Duke basketball is Elite 8-bound after beating St. John's in the Sweet 16 of the 2026 men's NCAA Tournament.The top-seeded Blue Devils (35-2) and head coach Jon Scheyer topped the five-seed Red Storm (30-7) and head coach Rick Pitino 80-75 from Capital One Arena in Washington, D.C.Duke's Isaiah Evans led all scorers with 25 points, while Cameron Boozer was on his heels with 22 points and 10 rebounds.The Fayetteville Observer provided live updates from the game. Check it out.Duke basketball vs St. John's live updatesBookmark this page for live updates from Duke basketball vs. St. John's. FINAL | Duke basketball advances to Elite 8Duke basketball hangs on down the stretch to beat St. John's 80-75 and punch its ticket to the Elite 8. Isaiah Evans goes to the lineIsaiah Evans goes 1-for-2 from the charity stripe, making it a 3-point game. St. John's heaves a 3-pointer, which hits nothing. Duke gets the ball under SJU's basket with 2.1 seconds to play. Dame Sarr sends Zuby Ejiofor to the lineA shooting foul on Sarr sends Ejiofor to the line, where he goes 1-for-2 to make it 77-75 in Duke's favor. Sarr grabs the rebound and St. John's is forced to foul with 11.2 seconds to play. Isaiah Evans will head to the line for the Blue Devils. St. John's Dylan Mitchell called for a holdDylan Mitchell is whistled for a hold against Cameron Boozer, whose 1-and-1 misses. Duke calls a timeoutJon Scheyer calls a timeout after St. John's cuts into the lead. Duke leads 77-74 with 40.7 seconds to play. St. John's calls a timeoutSt. John's calls a 30-second timeout with 1:07 to play. St. John's has one timeout and the possession arrow, while Duke has two timeouts and a five-point lead. Caleb Foster extends lead, only for St. John's to slash it in halfA long 2-pointer from Caleb Foster stretched Duke's lead out to six but a St. John's 3-pointer on the other end makes it a 3-point game with 1:56 to play. Cameron Boozer and-one, Duke back aheadCameron Boozer makes a layup and is fouled, putting Duke ahead 72-69 with 3:06 to go. Isaiah Evans seven straight points for Duke, Ian Jackson flagged for Flagrant 1Isaiah Evans has scored the last seven of Duke's points: a jumper, triple and layup. Its tied 65-all with 6:23 to go.Ian Jackson was flagged for a Flagrant 1 foul heading into the timeout, but Patrick Ngongba II missed both free throw attempts. Duke makes it a one possession gameCaleb Foster scored seven-straight points for the Blue Devils with three-straight buckets and a free throw. Cameron Boozer added a layup and its now a three point game, with St. John's leading 57-54 with 11:46 to go. Caleb Foster with back-to-back bucketsSt. John's went up by double digits for the first time of the night, and Caleb Foster responded with back-to-back buckets for the Blue Devils, who trail 55-49 at the 13:29 mark. Rick Pitino called timeout. St. John's kill shotThe Red Storm is on a 10-0 run and is up 50-44 with 16:26 to go. It's St. John's largest lead of the night. Duke, meanwhile, has turned it over three times in the last 2:40 and has been held scoreless.St. John's stretched its run to as much as 13-0. Two quick Duke turnovers to start second halfThat's back-to-back Duke turnovers in the halfcourt getting turned into Zuby Ejiofor dunks. St. John's leads 48-44 with 17:06 remaining. Halftime: St. John's 40, Duke 39The Johnnies take a 6-0 run into the half, holding Duke without a field goal for the last 4:43. Field goal drought for Duke, St. John's makes it a one possession gameThe Blue Devils haven't scored a field goal across the last 3:53 while St. John's has hit three in that span – all being triples. It's 39-37 Duke with 50.2 seconds left in the first half. The Johnnies are up to eight made 3's on the night. Duke uses 12-2 run to regain largest lead of nightDuke used a 12-2 run over the last three minutes, with five of the 12 points coming from Cameron Boozer, to take the 35-28 lead with 3:26 to go in the first half. A pair of Nik Khamenia free throws started the run for Duke.It marks Duke's largest lead of the night, having also been up by seven with 15 minutes in the period. St. John's holds lead at under-8 timeoutDuke tied the game off a Maliq Brown steal and ensuing Dame Sarr dunk, his first points of the game, but St. John's quickly responded with a Dillion Mitchell triple on its next possession to take the 26-23 lead. It was Mitchell's first made triple of the season. Jon Scheyer discusses Caleb Foster, St. John's pressure with Tracy WolfsonDuring an in-game interview with CBS reporter Tracy Wolfson, Duke coach Jon Scheyer was asked about Caleb Foster's return and St. John's defensive pressure."He's been a key guy for us. He's ready to go and we're gonna have him in there in quick spurts," Scheyer said of Foster.Scheyer said he likes when the Blue Devils "drive it strong" and they can't "be on their heels" against the Red Storm's defense. "We'll settle in and be better down there." St. John's hits three 3-pointers, takes lead vs Duke at under-12 timeoutSt. John's has turned up the pressure and knocked down a trio of 3-pointers to take a 19-15 lead vs. Duke with 11:51 left in the first half. Caleb Foster checks into the gameFor the first time since Duke's regular season finale vs. UNC, Caleb Foster is on the floor for the Blue Devils. St. John's quickly responds, tightens the gapFollowing Duke's 7-0 run, St. John's answers the call with five quick points as Dylan Darling drains a 3-pointer, followed by Dillon Mitchell stealing Duke's inbound pass and scoring a quick layup.Duke leads 11-9 at the first media timeout. Duke goes on 7-0 run to take early leadCameron Boozer kicks the ball out to twin brother Cayden Boozer, who hits a 3-pointer to stretch Duke's run out to seven unanswered points.The Blue Devils lead 11-4. Duke basketball starters vs St. John'sIt's Cayden Boozer, Isaiah Evans, Maliq Brown, Dame Sarr and Cameron Boozer making up Duke's starting five. Dylan Darling, Dillon Mitchell, Oziyah Sellers, Bryce Hopkins and Zuby Ejifor make up St. John's starting five. The game will be the first of the day in the East Regional, with No. 3 Michigan State set to take on the winner between No. 2 UConn and No. 7 UCLA at 9:45 p.m. ET on Friday.Duke vs St. John's predictionDuke 68, St. John's 65: Expect a defensive battle in Washington, D.C.
